stem.text: The function g is differentiable for all real numbers, and selected values of g and its derivative are given in the table. Find \( \lim_{x \to 2} \left(3 g(x) + 5\right) \), and justify your answer.

answer_key.label: The limit is 14, because g is differentiable at \( x = 2 \), so it is continuous there, and \( \lim_{x \to 2} g(x) = g(2) = 3 \).

worked_solution.text: g is differentiable at \( x = 2 \), so it is continuous there.
By the limit laws the limit is 3(3) + 5 = 14.
worked_solution.rule_named: sum and constant multiple limit laws

options.label: The limit is 14, because every function has its limit equal to its value at each input, and \( \lim_{x \to 2} g(x) = g(2) = 3 \).
options.derivation: the conclusion used as if it held for every function, with no hypothesis about g checked
